dublinCore.dc:title: 119 HR 9859 IH: Ethical Investigations and Integrity Act
dublinCore.dc:rights: Pursuant to Title 17 Section 105 of the United States Code, this file is not subject to copyright protection and is in the public domain.

action.action-desc: Mr. Messmer introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce

form.official-title: To require the Secretary of Labor to enter into adverse interest agreements if the Secretary shares information with an individual that is related to a potential civil action, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Ethical Investigations and Integrity Act.

subsection.text: In the event that the Secretary of Labor provides adverse assistance to an individual, prior to providing the adverse assistance, the Secretary shall—

paragraph.text: enter into a written agreement with the individual that details the nature and scope of such assistance; and
provide a copy of such agreement to any employer or contractor that may be directly and adversely impacted by such assistance.

Not later than 60 days after the date of enactment of this Act, and by December 31 of each year that begins after such date, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report containing information on all agreements to provide adverse assistance in effect for the preceding fiscal year, including, in relation to each such agreement—

subparagraph.text: a copy of the agreement, with any information described in subparagraph (2)(B) redacted;
the date the agreement was entered into; and
a detailed description of the nature and scope of the assistance provided during the fiscal year, including—

clause.text: the information shared, including the source, type, and amount of the information, and the date on which such information was shared;
a log of verbal communications, including—

subclause.text: the parties engaged in such communication;
the nature of any information shared; and
the parties present at the meeting;
the purpose of such meeting and the nature of any information shared.

subparagraph.text: shall identify the parties to each agreement; and
may not include any information that may be used to identify any other person (including an employer, contractor, or any other potential defendant).

subsection.text: For the purposes of subsection (a), if, not later than 60 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Labor takes the actions required in paragraphs (1) and (2) of such subsection in relation to an existing arrangement to provide adverse assistance, the Secretary shall be deemed to have taken such actions prior to providing such adverse assistance.

paragraph.text: The term adverse assistance means assistance or advice, including the disclosure of information, that is directed specifically toward an attorney for potential use in a civil action under any covered law.
The term covered law means any provision of law that is enforced by the Wage and Hour Division of the Department of Labor as of the date of enactment of this Act.
The term employer has the meaning given the term in section 3 of the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 (29 U.S.C. 203).
